newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany/U.S. sign aircraft safety checks agreement.
newsitem.headline: Germany/U.S. sign aircraft safety checks agreement.

text.p: The U.S. and German civil aviation authorities have agreed to accept each other's aircraft safety checks to reduce industry costs and red tape, the German transport ministry said.
The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (LBA) and the German Luftfahrt-Bundesamt (LBA) have signed an agreement on mutual recognition of aircraft safety monitoring, a ministry statement said.
The agreement was signed today at the 14th annual conference of the European Joint Aviation Authorities (JAA) and the FAA in Berlin.
Up to now, aircraft and components registered in the U.S. could be technically maintained by German firms only if these were checked, approved and monitored by the FAA.
The LBA is now the first European aviation authority whose controls will be recognised by the FAA, the ministry said.

German transport state secretary and aviation and aerospace co-ordinator, Norbert Lammert, said German maintenance companies would benefit from lower costs and less administration by only having a single authority responsible for checks.
The June 3-6 conference was attended by 300 experts from more than 30 countries who discussed safety standards, harmonisation of European flight operation rules and other technical matters.
